extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, farmers, industrialists, and policymakers (general public interested in industrial organization and rural industry)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive principles and practical criteria for decentralizing industry, designing and producing tractors/power-plants for farms, organizing factories for mass production, and structuring charity and employment so industry serves social good. Emphasis on seasonal reciprocity between farm and factory and on making power widely inexpensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity between farming and manufacturing
rubrics_metrics.description: A reciprocity can exist between farming and manufacturing. The manufacturer can give the farmer what he needs to be a good farmer, and the farmer and other producers of raw materials can give the manufacturer what he needs to be a good manufacturer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote mixed seasonal employment (farmers working in factories in dull farm seasons and builders/factory workers doing outdoor seasonal work) to remove 'slack times', restore balance between artificial and natural work, broaden minds, and reduce unrest caused by narrow, prejudiced judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate seasonal work to eliminate slack and waste
rubrics_metrics.description: Take the slack out of work and restore the balance between the artificial and the natural. The farm has its dull season — that is the time for the farmer to come into the factory; the factory also has its dull season — that is the time for the workmen to go out to the land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange teamwork and organizational structures enabling movement between seasonal occupations; resist forcing employees into continuous year-round single occupations when seasonal shifts would be more productive and healthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralization of industry over massive concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: The belief that an industrial country has to concentrate its industries is not well-founded. One can put a small plant on a little stream, and the combination of little plants, each making a single part, will make the whole cheaper than a vast factory would.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design industrial development to favor many small, specialized plants (single-product or single-part plants) when possible, locating them near resources and communities to avoid overcrowding and the social ills of great concentration. Note exceptions (e.g., casting) where large integrated plants may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small specialized plants as generally preferable
rubrics_metrics.description: Each plant making but one thing, with simple management and mechanism, avoids the need to search for skilled employees because the skill is in the machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor designs and processes that allow unskilled labor and machine-based skill, enabling countryside populations to split time between factory and farm; this supports decentralization and local livability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for integrated heavy processes (casting, metal work)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are exceptions, as where casting has to be done. In such cases we want to combine the making of the metal and the casting of it and also we want to use all of the waste power. This requires a large investment and a considerable force of men in one place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize technical/economic exceptions where centralization is justified; do not force decentralization where process economics demand integrated scale (e.g., heavy metallurgy, casting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of cheap, convenient central power as essential infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: There ought to be a central station to furnish cheap power--it ought to be held as essential as a railway or a water supply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harness local power sources (hydro-electric, steam at mine mouth, etc.) as community utilities; low-cost power is a primary enabler of decentralization and reduced living/doing-business overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise notions about capital: capital must create jobs and service
rubrics_metrics.description: Capital that a business makes for itself, that is employed to expand the workman's opportunity and increase his comfort and prosperity ... is not a menace to humanity. Capital that is not constantly creating more and better jobs is more useless than sand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate capital by its social use: priorities should be job creation, better conditions of labor, and making money do more service for the betterment of life, rather than mere private accumulation. Hold surplus in trust for business continuity and worker welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tractor design principle: light, strong, simple, cheap, and producible
rubrics_metrics.description: The only kind of tractor worth working on was one that would be light, strong, and so simple that any one could run it. Also it had to be so cheap that any one could buy it. Each part had to be as strong as it was possible to make it, the parts had to be few in number, and the whole had to admit of quantity production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design agricultural machinery prioritizing minimal parts, robustness, simplicity of operation, and mass-producibility to drive down price and broaden adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tractor functional specifics (pulling, grip, engine, versatility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The automobile is designed to carry; the tractor is designed to pull--to climb. The grip is in the lugs on the driving wheels. We fixed upon a four-cylinder engine that is started by gasoline but runs thereafter on kerosene. In addition ... it had also to be designed for work as a stationary engine ... a compact, versatile power plant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineer tractors for traction (not weight), clutch/grip design (lugs/spuds), dual-fuel operation for economy, and adaptability to stationary-belt-driven tasks; design for varied implements and terrains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing organization for mass tractor production
rubrics_metrics.description: The mechanism of the tractor is even more simple than that of the automobile and it is manufactured in exactly the same fashion ... Each part is a separate departmental undertaking and each part as it is finished joins the conveyor system which leads it to its proper initial assembly and eventually into the final assembly. Everything moves and there is no skilled work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use departmentalized parts production, conveyor assembly, and unskilled/semiskilled labor to achieve high throughput and cost reductions; set up a separate plant for each distinct article rather than mixing product types in one plant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price reduction through scientific/large-scale production
rubrics_metrics.description: What getting into scientific production will do to a price ... the capacity of the present plant is one million tractors a year. That is the number we expect to make ... the first tractors ... were first offered ... at $750 ... with River Rouge plant functioning we were able to cut to $395.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale and process improvements (specialized plant, conveyorized assembly, parts simplification) are primary levers for reducing unit price and making power accessible to all farms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance and field trial metrics for tractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial results: cross-ploughing on measured acre occupied 1 hour 30 minutes, with a consumption of 2 gallons of paraffin per acre. Total weight fully loaded was 23 1/4 cwts. The tractor is light for its power, easily handled, turns in a small circle, and leaves a very narrow headland. The motor is quickly started up from cold on a small supply of petrol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate tractors by field trial metrics: acres per hour, fuel consumption per acre, weight on land, maneuverability (turning circle, headland width), cold-start reliability, and suitability of implements (plough compatibility). Provide recommendations (e.g., stronger driving-wheels if needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic comparison metric: cost per acre (tractor vs horses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost of ploughing with Fordson, per acre .95 (including depreciation, repairs, fuel, oil, driver). Cost of ploughing with horses, per acre 1.46 (including depreciation, feed, drivers). The tractor ploughing is done in about one fourth the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full-cost accounting per acre (depreciation over expected life, repairs, fuel, oil, labor) and time-efficiency to compare mechanized power vs animal labor; include time element benefits even when some cost items vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power-farming as removal of drudgery and viability condition for farms
rubrics_metrics.description: Power-farming is simply taking the burden from flesh and blood and putting it on steel ... Within a few years a farm depending solely on horse and hand power will be as much of a curiosity as a factory run by a treadmill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt mechanization broadly so that farms become efficient food businesses rather than purely labor occupations; anticipate drastically reduced manual labor days and repurposing of labor time for other business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local cooperative processing and reduced centralization of food manufacturing
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperative farming will become so developed that we shall see associations of farmers with their own packing houses ... a revival of the small flour-milling business ... Why a steer raised in Texas should be brought to Chicago and then served in Boston is a question that cannot be answered as long as all the steers the city needs could be raised near Boston.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage cooperative local value-added facilities (mills, packing houses) to reduce transportation/organization waste and to keep food production and processing near points of consumption when economically feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the high overhead of great cities; favor livable smaller communities
rubrics_metrics.description: The overhead expense of living or doing business in the great cities is becoming so large as to be unbearable ... The modern city has been prodigal, it is to-day bankrupt, and to-morrow it will cease to be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for municipal indebtedness, interest costs, and maintenance of complex infrastructure when assessing the value of city concentration; favor decentralized communities with lower overhead and seasonal harmony with nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charity should aim to remove need and promote self-reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If human sympathy prompts us to feed the hungry, why should it not give the larger desire--to make hunger in our midst impossible? The charitable system that does not aim to make itself unnecessary is not performing service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design philanthropic efforts to address root causes of poverty and to create productive employment opportunities rather than merely providing temporary relief. Avoid professionalized, systematized charity that degrades recipients and fosters dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to professionalized charity and sentimental social service
rubrics_metrics.description: I have no patience with professional charity ... The moment human helpfulness is systematized, organized, commercialized, and professionalized, the heart of it is extinguished ... Whole sections of our population were coddled into a state of expectant, child-like helplessness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor informal, community-based mutual aid and social structures that preserve dignity and self-respect; be wary of institutionalized 'social service' that creates dependence or resentment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivision of industry to absorb the maimed, halt, and blind
rubrics_metrics.description: The subdivision of industry opens places which can be filled by the maimed, the halt, and the blind ... There are more places in subdivision industry that can be filled by blind men than there are blind men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize production tasks into fine-grained operations so that persons with limited abilities can be employed productively; avoid wasting potential by assigning inappropriate tasks to able-bodied workers that could be done by those less able.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prisons as potentially productive units (with safeguards)
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-conducted jail should not only be self-supporting, but a man in jail ought to be able to support his family ... I am not advocating convict labour or the farming out of men practically as slaves ... But as long as we have prisons they can be fitted into the general scheme of production so neatly that a prison may become a productive unit working for the relief of the public and the benefit of the prisoners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame prison industry policy so that work trains inmates, produces value for public benefit, and helps reintegration rather than exploiting labor; remove legal restrictions enacted at the behest of narrow interests that harm community welfare.
